questions: What is the exact definition of "decomposing a tree into paths" - must every edge belong to exactly one path, or can edges be shared between paths?
Can paths share vertices, or must all vertices in the decomposition be disjoint across different paths?
Is a path allowed to visit the same vertex more than once within a single path of length K?
What should be the output format if K=1, since paths of length 1 don't have meaningful connectivity requirements?
How should self-loops or multiple edges be handled, even though the constraints suggest they won't appear?
What is the precise meaning of "length K" - does it refer to the number of edges (K-1) or the number of vertices (K) in the path?
Are the paths required to be simple paths (no repeated vertices), or can they backtrack?
What happens when N=0 or K=0 - should these edge cases be considered valid inputs given the constraint specifications?

inline_prompts: You are given a tree with NK vertices. The vertices are numbered 1,2,\dots,NK, and the i-th edge (i=1,2,\dots,NK-1) connects vertices u_i and v_i bidirectionally. Determine whether this tree can be decomposed into N paths, each of length K. More precisely, determine whether there exists an N \times K matrix P satisfying the following: For each i=1,2,\dots,N and j=1,2,\dots,K-1, there is an edge connecting vertices P_{i,j} and P_{i,j+1}. Note that the decomposition requires that every vertex is included in exactly one path. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K u_1 v_1 u_2 v_2 \vdots u_{NK-1} v_{NK-1} Output If it is possible to decompose the tree into N paths each of length K, print Yes. Constraints - 1 \leq N - 1 \leq K - NK \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq u_i < v_i \leq NK - The given graph is a tree. - All input values are integers.
